primary_diagnosis: Graves disease with thyroid eye disease
recommended_management: agranulocytosis safety netting - seek urgent full blood count if sore throat or fever
interpretation: Unequivocal primary thyrotoxicosis. The strongly positive TRAb with increased homogeneous uptake and a raised thyroglobulin confirms Graves disease and excludes destructive thyroiditis and exogenous hormone.
The patient has an overactive thyroid.
Graves disease. Proceed to definitive treatment promptly.

key_findings: dopamine and hydrocortisone both suppress TSH
recommended_management: repeat testing after recovery in six weeks as an outpatient
interpretation: The raised reverse T3 with an intact cortisol response distinguishes non-thyroidal illness from central hypothyroidism. Levothyroxine is not indicated.
Low free T4 with an inappropriately normal TSH indicates central hypothyroidism. Thyroid hormone replacement is indicated. There is a risk of thyroid storm if untreated.

key_findings: normal INR and fibrinogen excluding DIC
recommended_tests: adamts13 activity and inhibitor before exchange
recommended_management: urgent plasma exchange immediately, do not wait for adamts13
interpretation: PLASMIC score 6 with schistocytes and a normal coagulation screen. Start plasma exchange within hours; the ADAMTS13 sample must be drawn before exchange.

recommended_management: transfuse platelets to correct the count
await the adamts13 result before starting plasma exchange
interpretation: Likely TTP. Correct the thrombocytopenia and confirm with ADAMTS13.

key_findings: VNTR shows the same strain - relapse not reinfection
no tenderness so not a reaction
recommended_tests: slit-skin smear with bacterial and morphological index
molecular resistance testing of rpob folp1 gyra
interpretation: A rising bacterial index with viable bacilli and an rpoB mutation is relapse with acquired rifampicin resistance, not a reaction.
The patient is deteriorating on treatment, which indicates drug resistance. Escalate to second-line therapy.

key_findings: clinically euthyroid with bradycardia and weight gain
results normal on an alternative platform
TRAb negative discordant with the pattern
recommended_management: advise holding biotin before future tests including troponin
interpretation: The patient is clinically euthyroid and bradycardic. Biotin interferes with streptavidin-biotin immunoassays, lowering sandwich assays and raising competitive ones. Note biotin also affects other assays such as troponin.
